_note: Prompt 112. Advisory frame-time and heap thresholds per profile, recorded so a change can be compared with them by hand. The `profiles` below are NOT enforced by CI or by any test: a shared runner measures its own load (the documented rule). The `deviceProfiles` block at the end is enforced by e2e/deviceProfiles.spec.js (Prompt 285), by budgets with room for that load. frameMs is the mean time between animation frames with the frame-rate cap lifted, so it is a throughput figure for light scenes (compositor and GPU bound, see OFFLINE_AND_LOW_END.md) and a script figure for heavy ones. A frame threshold is the measured value times 1.5, rounded up to 0.5 ms; a heap threshold is the measured used heap after a forced collection times 1.5, rounded up to 1 MB (a scenario's first visit loads its code, so compare the used heap, not the growth). Real-device profiles are empty until someone fills them from real hardware.

computation.note: Prompt 285. What the quality tier does to computation: the size each heavy computation takes at each tier. js/quality.js mirrors these values (a static page cannot read tools/) and tests/computeTier.test.js holds the two equal. A kernel never reads them: a kernel takes its size as an argument and gives the same numbers on both tiers for the same argument; the caller (a panel, a record) asks js/quality.js for the argument and says so in the result's provenance when it was reduced. `tolerance` is what the low tier's result may differ from the full tier's, stated before the validators ran; `adopters` names the one file each key is read in.

tolerance.bootstrapDraws: the bootstrap standard error is within 15 percent of the full tier's (its own sampling error is 1/sqrt(2(B-1)): 4.1 percent at 300 draws, 2.2 at 1000, so 15 percent is 3 times the combined error)
tolerance.monteCarloDraws: each end of the mass sum's 68 and 95 percent intervals is within 3 percent of the interval's width of the full tier's
tolerance.profilePoints: each end of a profile interval is within 5 percent of the interval's half-width of the full tier's
tolerance.workerConcurrency: none: a cap on realms at once changes the time, never a number
tolerance.workerMemoryBytes: none: a cap on bytes held changes what waits, never a number

deviceProfiles.note: Prompt 285. Three automated profiles, ENFORCED by e2e/deviceProfiles.spec.js in CI (the older `profiles` above stay advisory). PROXIES: a CPU throttle on the main thread only (a Worker, the compositor and the GPU run at the host's speed), a V8 heap ceiling (it bounds JavaScript memory, not decoded images, canvases or GPU memory) and a network shape (a rate and a delay, not a radio). Not one of them is a device: the real-device profiles below stay empty and every real-device claim stays UNKNOWN in tools/evidence-status.json. A time budget is the measured value times 3, rounded up to 100 ms, and never under 4000 ms; a heap budget is the measured used heap after a forced collection times 2, rounded up to 1 MB, and never under 8 MB: a shared runner has its own load, and a budget it can fail by being busy would be a report on the runner. Each is set from a measurement and never loosened to pass. The heap figure is small because the Observatory's data is small; the budget is for a regression that holds frames and tables it should have let go.
